result.title: HarnessPro: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement with Pareto Optimization for Performance-Cost Trade-offs
result.summary: Harness development plays a crucial role in building capable AI agents. Recent approaches improve harnesses through recursive self-improvement (RSI), but their performance gains often come with higher execution costs. We introduce HarnessPro, a label-free method for evolving harnesses to improve task performance while reducing execution cost. In this setting, candidate harnesses are evaluated using LLM-generated tests without access to ground-truth solutions or official tests. Specialized agents diagnose execution trajectories, plan updates with different performance-cost priorities, and implement them as candidate harnesses. Rather than returning a single harness, HarnessPro uses normalized weighted squared-distance selection to provide cost-focused (lite), balanced (medium), and performance-focused (heavy) harnesses for different deployment budgets. Selected harnesses enter the next iteration, where execution feedback guides further updates. Our experiments cover Terminal-Bench 2, SWE-Bench Pro, and ProgramBench, using GPT-5.5 with Codex and GLM-5.2 with Claude Code. Across these benchmarks using GPT-5.5 with Codex, the heavy mode of HarnessPro achieves an average pass-rate gain of 2.0 percentage points and an average per-task cost reduction of 26.1% relative to RHO. This advantage also holds when using GLM-5.2 with Claude Code. Code is available at https://github.com/pzs19/HarnessPro

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 HarnessPro，一种无需标注的 agent harness 递归自我改进方法：由专门 agent 诊断执行轨迹、按不同性能-成本偏好实现候选 harness，并用归一化加权平方距离选择出 lite/medium/heavy 三档方案，在 Terminal-Bench 2 等基准上同时提升通过率并降低单任务成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按性能-成本权衡进行 Pareto 式候选选择、并以轨迹诊断反馈驱动迭代的做法，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的收益-成本预算分配与无真值条件下的轨迹监督提供方法线索，但具体迁移需核查原文。
